children: was initiated with a Buy rating by Truist Securities due in part to its engineering talent and new contract economics that could provide upside to pricing and revenue.

"We view Nebius as an opportunity to invest in a scaling AI-native hyperscaler still building out its infrastructure," said Truist analyst Arvind Ramnani in a Wednesday investor report. "We believe consensus forecasts for 2027E ARR are conservative given recent pricing ($20-25M/MW for 1-3 year deals, $40-50M/MW for shorter duration) and are modeling 2027E ARR well above consensus."

"We see significant opportunity ahead for Nebius and estimate a $2.1T annual revenue opportunity at the cloud layer by 2030E," he added. "We see scarcity and contract economics supporting upside to pricing and revenue, and we see multiple paths to reach 20-30% adjusted EBIT margins over the medium term."
Truist set a $355 price target on the stock.
The financial firm believes Nebuis can capture market share from fellow neoclouds as well as from the large hyperscalers.

"We believe this engineering talent (850+ engineers) along with M&A provide Neblus with an advantageous position to move up the stack and capture inference workload opportunities, which we expect to comprise a significant majority of AI workloads in the years ahead," Ramnani noted.
Nebius' CEO and founder, Arkady Volozh, also founded Yandex.

title: Nebius receives Buy rating as recent cloud economics provide revenue upside: Truist
